t.6.112.1: When the fourteenth year was complete, on the fifth day, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa reached the hermitage of Bharadvāja and, self-restrained, bowed in reverence to the sage.
t.6.112.2: Having saluted Bharadvāja, rich in austerity, he asked him: “Blessed one, do you hear anything of plenty and good health in the city? Is Bharata diligent in his duties, and are my mothers still living?”
t.6.112.3: Thus addressed by Rāma, the great sage Bharadvāja, smiling first and as if overjoyed, replied to the best of the Raghus.
t.6.112.4: Bharata, smeared with mud and wearing matted locks, awaits you, having placed your sandals before him; and all is well at home.
t.6.112.5: You, who long ago, clad in garments of bark, entered the great forest with a woman as the third of your company, fallen from your kingdom and desiring dharma alone...
t.6.112.6: Him who stood on foot, who had given up all he possessed and carried out his father's word, bereft of heavenly enjoyments, like an immortal fallen from heaven.
t.6.112.8: Now, beholding you with your purpose fully accomplished, surrounded by your friends, your hosts and your kinsmen, and with your enemy vanquished, my joy is unsurpassed.
t.6.112.7: Formerly, O conqueror in battle, compassion arose in me when I saw you, bound by Kaikeyī's word, living on wild roots and fruits.
t.6.112.9: O Rāghava, all your joy and sorrow is known to me, the great measure of it that you have met with, beginning with the slaughter at Janasthāna.
t.6.112.11: The sight of Kabandha, and likewise the journey to Pampā, your friendship with Sugrīva, and how Vālī was slain by you.
t.6.112.10: While he was engaged in the service of the brāhmaṇas, protecting all the ascetics, there came the sighting of Mārīca and also the violent abduction of Sītā.
t.6.112.13: And how Rāvaṇa, the thorn of the gods, was slain in battle together with his sons, kinsmen and ministers, with his army and with his mounts.
t.6.112.12: The search for Vaidehī and the deed of the son of the Wind; how, once Vaidehī had been found, Nala's bridge was built; and how Laṅkā was set ablaze by the exultant leaders of the monkey troops.
t.6.112.14: Your meeting with the thirty gods, and how the boon was granted to you, all this is known to me through my austerity, O lover of dharma.
t.6.112.15: I too grant you a boon here, O best of weapon-bearers. Accept this guest-offering; tomorrow you will go to Ayodhyā.
t.6.112.16: Receiving those words of his with a bow of the head, the glorious prince, overjoyed, said "Very well" and asked for a boon.
t.6.112.18: The fruit-bearing trees became fruitless, those rich in flowers became flowerless, and those trees that were full of leaves and dripping with honey withered away.
t.6.112.17: O blessed one, along the road as I go toward Ayodhyā, may the trees bear fruit even out of season, and may all of them flow with honey.
